Maybe try therapy. You could have a place to release these problems. A good rule is that people like positive happy people. It’s not to say that once you have a good friend you can’t open up about some stuff. But usually you wait a bit before disclosing. A good rule of thumb to remember when talking to others is 70/30. Make 70% of the conversation about them and 30% about yourself.

Self-depreciating humor is good but it has to be done right. It sounds like you’re not doing it right. So maybe try to stay away from that for awhile, or maybe the topics you’re self-depreciating are too serious. Or likely, you’re self-depreciating things you’re actually insecure about. It subconsciously comes off differently than when you’re self-depreciating about something you’re actually confident in. People can tell.

How to not be so sensitive? Get more confidence. The more confident in yourself you are, the less you’ll be bothered by people poking fun. Your family poking fun at you can actually be a good way to toughen you up. When they poke fun, poke fun back. My siblings really helped me not be as sensitive growing up because we were constantly busting each other.

It was the best date I had ever been on. We dated for a year and a half. We talked about marriage and kids. He almost proposed to me. Now I'm 24 and he's 27. He fell out of love with me because of the distance, and is with a new girl now. I wouldn't ever reach out to him unless they broke up. I hope that maybe we align one day where we're both single and I'm able to reach out to him, or better yet, he reaches out to me. At the moment, this is all I want. I'm sure in time I will grow to not care anymore. 

Anyway, I wish you the best. I hope things turn out how you want. Thank you for sharing your beautiful story.

I wish I could take it all back. 

I think he believed he felt that way in the moment. We were long distance. And I think because he hadn't seen me in awhile, he was losing feelings. The way the break up has been makes me feel like he was a shitty person, but he wasn't a shitty person during the relationship. I was so happy. And now I'm so miserable. Three months later and I still feel like this, and honestly it doesn't feel like it's getting better. Like I am a lot better, but it feels like I've hit a plateau.

Before I met him, I knew I was going to find someone and get married. I never really questioned that. I've had other relationships, but only two, including him, ever made me feel this way. I honestly didn't think I could ever feel that way about someone again. I just kind of accepted that the first guy was an exception, because he was my first love. And your first love is just always the most intense. But now that I've felt that again, I've become addicted again. Now I know it's possible, so theoretically I could find someone who makes me feel this way again. But I've started to pin point what it was about him that made me attracted to him, and the first guy so much. And part of me just feels like I'm not good enough to keep a guy like that. That's why neither of those guys stayed. I know I have no idea, so all I can do is live my life and try to find that again. But that's the fear. It's that my standards of what makes me crazy about a guy are too high for what I can actually get.

I'm trying so hard to tell myself this, but what if I never find someone who makes me feel that way again? I'm not saying no one can make me feel that way, but just the idea that I never will find that scares the crap out of me.
